title: Kem Kem beds, home of Spinosaurus
summary: The Kem Kem Group of eastern Morocco, made of the lower Gara Sbaa and upper Douira formations, holds Cenomanian-age deltaic sediments with a fauna of large theropods that includes Spinosaurus. A partial Spinosaurus aegyptiacus skeleton was found by a local collector at Zrigat, about 20 km north of Erfoud, and isolated Spinosaurus teeth are reported from the Gara Sbaa Formation. Juvenile spinosaurines are also described from these beds.

uncertainty.note: Range from Table 7 of the ZooKeys monograph; its text says the age of initial deposition is best estimated as Early Cenomanian. The id says 95 Ma; no opened page gives 95. Years are Ma counted back from the present.

as_recorded.value: the middle Cretaceous (Cenomanian) Kem Kem beds of Morocco

where.modern_name: Kem Kem region near Erfoud, Errachidia Province, eastern Morocco (proxy pin at Erfoud; Zrigat is about 20 km north)
where.historical_name: Kem Kem Group deltaic basin, northwestern Gondwana (Africa), Cenomanian; no polities exist

paleo.note: Erfoud proxy at 96 Ma. MULLER2019 gives 12.92 N, 9.42 W and PALEOMAP 18.84 N, 4.48 W at 95 Ma, so the models disagree by about 10 degrees.

importance.justification: A well-studied Cenomanian deposit that yields Spinosaurus and other large theropods.
